shared_contracts.asn1_item_callbacks: An `ASN1_AUX.asn1_cb` is reached only through the `funcs` of the one `ASN1_ITEM` that declares it, and the item machinery allocates and validates the value with that item's `size`; therefore the callback's `*pval` cast is fixed by the registrar entry, not by the input bytes. Freeing: FREE_PRE runs before the template walk (the callback owns non-template members of the selected arm), FREE_POST runs after it (the walk has released and NULLed every template field, so the callback owns non-template members only and a template-field release is a no-op).
shared_contracts.sk_free_thunks: The crate's stacks are untyped, so an element destructor is reached through a `void *`-shaped thunk. The obligation is the stack's element type; it holds because each stack is grown only by this crate's own constructor, which pushes the element only after a successful construction and transfers one reference to the list.
shared_contracts.provider_dispatch: A provider dispatch entry is published by a table in the same translation unit as the constructor, and the core supplies the method's own `provctx` (`ossl_provider_ctx(prov)`). The answer is owned by the caller and released by the same table's `freectx`.
shared_contracts.ex_data_free: `CRYPTO_free_ex_data` invokes each registered index's free hook exactly once per object teardown, with the slot's current value (NULL included). An index's free hook may therefore assume only `ptr` NULL-or-the-type-this-crate-stores-at-that-index, and must own the release it performs.
shared_contracts.cleanup_stack: `engine_cleanup_add_last` records a `void (*)(void)`; the runner `engine_cleanup_int` is withheld, so a registered callback is unreachable in this candidate. Both engine rows state the lock precondition the runner will owe.

rows.obligation: `ENGINE_CLEANUP_CB`'s ABI rule plus this callback's own two preconditions: the engine lock is initialised and is not held by the calling thread (`ENGINE_remove` takes it). Both are established by the only path that can make the list non-empty: `ENGINE_add` -> `engine_list_add`, whose engine came from `ENGINE_new`/`ENGINE_by_id`, and both run `run_engine_lock_init` (ENGINE_new, src/engine/eng_lib.rs:441-445).
rows.evidence: The contract was already present and correct; the row is discharged on the registration and the reachability fact rather than on a new document line. With a NULL lock the loop's `ENGINE_remove` answers 0 and the function returns with the list intact - a leak, not UB, which the contract states.

findings_note: No memory-safety defect was found in the 22 sites: every obligation is the documentation gap the census names, plus one eliminate-able duplicate declaration. Two near-defects were checked and are recorded as observations rather than findings, so a reviewer can replay the check rather than trust the conclusion.

observations.class: authority-shaped hazard that is sound only because of an adjacent rule
observations.where: cms_kemri_cb FREE_POST releases `ukm`, which *is* a template field (src/cms/cms_asn1.rs:1926-1945, offset 48).
observations.why_sound: `template_free` -> `item_embed_free(embed = 0)` -> `primitive_free` clears the caller's slot at src/asn1/fre.rs:186-187, so the field is NULL before FREE_POST and `ASN1_STRING_free(NULL)` is a no-op.
observations.why_recorded: The authority writes the same shape (crypto/cms/cms_asn1.c:186-203). It is not a defect, but the safety of this row is one edit away from being wrong: if the free walk ever stopped clearing field slots, this callback would double-release a secret-bearing octet string. B56-C3 is that edit's tripwire.
observations.disposition: PINNED by B56-C3; no code change (matching the authority is required).

observations.class: layout-robust type confusion that a behaviour test cannot see
observations.why_recorded: Both callbacks cast the looked-up method to their own type; `EvpCipher` and `EvpMd` both begin with the NID `int`, so swapping the two registrations would keep the added names identical. A behaviour test therefore cannot be the control; the installation site and the declared element type are.

new_unsafe_assumptions_note: No unsafe fn was added and no exported item changed. The test code adds six unsafe blocks in `#[cfg(test)]` units (each with a `SAFETY:` comment) and no non-test unsafe operation; one production unsafe extern block was removed.
boundary_size: Four mechanisms, 22 sites: 8 ASN.1 item callbacks (6 CMS + 1 PKCS7 + 1 internal shutdown), 4 concurrency sites (2 OBJ_NAME walk callbacks, 2 cfg-variant lock releasers), 8 provider sites (2 stack thunks, 1 provider-ABI constructor, 1 provider-list thunk, 1 key-state predicate, 1 digest init, 1 extern block eliminated, 1 decoder free thunk) and 2 C ABI callbacks (one ex_data free hook, one cleanup callback). 20 fn-level contracts added (the 21st discharged row, engine_list_cleanup, already carried a correct one); 7 controls (5 allocator/witness controls, 2 compile-time/behavioural); 5 production mutations each observed FAILED and reverted byte-for-byte. No new unsafe abstraction.
safe_callers_can_cause_ub_note: Every row is either an `unsafe extern "C"` callback installed by the crate's own registration (item `funcs`, stack destructor slot, provider dispatch entry, ex_data index, cleanup stack), an internal `unsafe fn` with no safe caller, or - for the eliminated row - a declaration that no longer exists. No safe Rust item accepts or returns any of these types, so a safe caller cannot reach them; the retained obligations are C-ABI caller duties, stated per row.

residuals.description: The element type of every stack destructor/dup thunk is the stack writer's obligation. It is established for the in-crate stacks (decoder_insts, encoder_insts, activated_providers) by their single constructors, but a future writer that pushes another type would not be caught by the type system. B56-C6 pins the ABI shape, not the element type.

cms_kemri_cb's free of the template field `ukm` is a no-op only because the free walk clears field slots (B56-O1). B56-C3 fails if the clearing is removed; there is no production change, because matching the authority is required.

Three rows are discharged with no in-candidate caller: ossl_rand_cleanup_int (shutdown exclusion), sha512_224_init (live/unique context) and engine_list_cleanup (engine lock initialised and not held). Their landing callers owe those preconditions; the rows say so, and no safe Rust path reaches them today.
No authority differential, sanitizer or Miri run; no leak measurement for the CMS free callbacks' partial-build paths. The controls measure single release by address, not leak-freedom.
B56-O2: the two namemap walk callbacks are layout-agnostic under a swap, so the discharge rests on the installation site and the declared element type rather than on a behaviour test.
`decoder_instance_free_thunk` exists twice (src/decoder_pkey.rs:587 and src/decoder_meth.rs:774) with identical bodies. Both are correct; consolidating them is a cleanup outside this sweep's scope.

non_claims: B56 scopes its 21 discharges to the named operations and their callers; none of the four mechanisms is discharged mechanism-wide, and the two X509 rows B55-F1 blocks stay BLOCKED.
No row is counted as discharged on documentation alone: each row names the caller or ABI rule that supplies its argument and the fact that makes the operation sound.
The controls prove registration and single release by allocator address; they do not prove leak-freedom, DER equality, or constant-time behaviour.
The candidate is HEAD plus an uncommitted delta; a reviewer must freeze that delta as S' before applying.
UNSAFE_EXTERN_BLOCK elimination reused an existing declaration; it does not claim that the crate's libc surface is otherwise verified.
